about: The growth map (doc 128, principle `amoeba`). Each capability declares the simplest living form it ships in (the amoeba — one person, no server, offline), the stages it can grow into, the CONDITIONS that trigger each stage (favourable: more nodes/teams/traffic/resources; unfavourable: load, failure, a lost node — antifragile), and the RAIL already built into the amoeba so the next form can self-assemble. Actuation is graded: 'auto' steps are safe, reversible and in-box (the estate may do them itself); 'assisted' steps provision infrastructure, cost money or touch endpoints and stay behind a human's ./securax approve. ./securax evolve senses the current conditions and names what is ready to grow and the one step to grow it. This file is DATA; every enterprise-capable feature should carry an entry (fitness evolution-declared ratchets the count up, never down). Seeded with the capabilities whose rails are built; extend it as each feature grows its seam.

conditions.about: How the estate reads its own conditions, honestly and locally — no telemetry leaves the box.

signals.nodes: how many reference/sync nodes are live (governance/resilience.py reference; 1 = a lone amoeba)
signals.gateway: a model gateway is configured (GATEWAY_URL) — the estate can think, not only react
signals.fleet_server: a Velociraptor/endpoint server is configured (a standing organism, not a one-off collector)
signals.internal_mirror: an internal tool/registry mirror is set (SECURAX_HUNT_MIRROR) — mass deployment without vendor egress
signals.teams: more than one team/tenant uses the estate (platform tenancy in use)
signals.load: sustained load or repeated incidents — a stress signal that the amoeba form is being outgrown
signals.lost_node: a node went down — fall back to the amoeba form (no-SPOF), then regrow when it returns

hunt.organism: an offline Velociraptor collector on one host or in the pipeline — no server

stages.is: offline collector, no server, one host / DevSecOps pipeline; deterministic triage

stages.grows_to: a Velociraptor server with clients, fleet-wide hunts, throttling
stages.rail: ./securax hunt fleet generates the server setup, the client rollout (GPO/Intune/SCCM/Ansible) and a throttled fleet hunt — the SAME packs run unchanged; provisions nothing (approved steps)

stages.grows_to: a managed fleet with per-team RBAC and multi-org tenancy, an org-governed tool mirror with EULA acceptance, scheduled hunts, AI-agent triage and drafted remediation behind approval
stages.rail: ./securax hunt fleet points binaries at SECURAX_HUNT_MIRROR (no vendor egress); Velociraptor's built-in RBAC/multi-org maps to the rbac/tenancy/policy platform services; the gated-tool EULA-acceptance ledger; the approve workflow

unfavourable.lost_node: the fleet server is a natural SPOF — on its loss, fall back to the offline-collector amoeba, which needs no server; regrow when it returns

crisis.organism: a single responder tracking one agency requisition in the local vault

stages.is: one person, the register and the ready documents, runs offline in the vault

stages.grows_to: per-team owners and SPOCs, the chase routine nudging each team, shared runs across nodes
stages.rail: every requisition item already carries an owning team; the crisis-watch routine; the read-only mirror of the clock to every node

stages.grows_to: shared requisition runs with SLA timers and escalation, a war-room roster, an org-governed template library, AI-drafted filings behind approval
stages.rail: the audit/export/rbac platform services; the approve gate for anything that leaves the building

unfavourable.lost_node: a live requisition lives in the node's vault and the backups; track it on the always-on node or restore the vault

wargame.organism: a lone responder running a scored tabletop from the local vault

stages.is: one person, deterministic scoring, no gateway, runs offline

stages.grows_to: model-graded free text and an AI-played sender under the governed rails
stages.rail: the gateway call is already wired and degrades to the rubric when absent

stages.grows_to: shared multi-player runs with a facilitator and live team scoreboards, an org-governed scenario library, after-action reports rolled into the exercise programme
stages.rail: the scenarios are data; runs are per-node and replicate; the export/audit services

unfavourable.load: when coordination keeps failing a scenario, the after-action report turns each gap into a standing lesson and a drill — the stress makes the next run stronger

evolve.organism: a read-only growth map on one node: senses conditions, recommends, proposes the rail

stages.is: senses local conditions and shows what is ready to grow; does nothing on its own

stages.grows_to: the estate performs the safe, in-box growth steps itself (enable a toggle, arm a routine, add a model rung) when conditions warrant
stages.rail: each stage already carries an `actuation` grade; the auto-graded steps are the safe seam to actuate

stages.grows_to: org-wide growth governance: a fleet-level view, policy over which capabilities may auto-grow, scheduled condition-driven scaling under the approval workflow
stages.rail: the policy platform service; the approve workflow; the per-capability actuation grades

unfavourable.lost_node: it holds no state and runs from the code, so any node answers; nothing to recover

guiding-map.organism: the Life OS on one device: its data in that browser, working offline, opened from wherever it was installed

stages.is: one device, data in the browser, works offline; it depended on the one machine that served it

stages.grows_to: hosted as a static site so it opens on every device with no machine of yours running, and synced across devices through your own encrypted OneDrive copy
stages.rail: tools/pwa_publish.py publishes it with the site (doc 130); OneDrive sync with a passphrase (doc 72); node-to-node sync (doc 86); the hosted door finds a live node (doc 131)

stages.grows_to: an organisation's own address behind its sign-in, one person per account, a shared hub node, SSO
stages.rail: Cloudflare Access in front of the app (doc 72, doc 85); the identity and tenancy platform services; hub sync

unfavourable.lost_node: the hosted copy and the device copy both keep working with every machine of yours off; data returns from OneDrive sync or an exported backup

gateway.organism: a local/free model behind the rails, serving one person with zero external calls

stages.is: one node, a local model, the rails + allowance + audit chain, offline-capable

stages.grows_to: a provider ladder with failover and a kill switch across nodes
stages.rail: the model ladder and the kill switch are already in the config; add a rung

stages.grows_to: per-team allowances and metering, tenant isolation, an organisation-governed policy
stages.rail: the identity/tenancy/metering/policy platform services the gateway already speaks to

unfavourable.lost_node: answers fall back along the ladder to a local model; no single provider or node is the dependency

threat-news.organism: a threat-intelligence engine that keeps a person, a family or an organisation rehearsed against what is happening in the world now

stages.is: open feeds read daily on the build server, matched to a curated library, one static pack next to the hosted Life OS, rehearsals on the device

stages.grows_to: a local model reads each headline, explains it in plain words and fits the drill to the person's own profile on the device, never sending the profile
stages.rail: the pack already carries ids, heat and headlines; the gateway's local model and the device profile are the inputs

stages.grows_to: community reports ('I saw this scam'), an organisation's own sources and patterns, STIX/TAXII and MISP exchange, per tenant
stages.rail: sources and patterns are data files with ids; the pack is a versioned contract

unfavourable.lost_node: the drills are bundled in the app; with no pack or no network the Life OS still shows every threat and drill, only without headlines
